rationale: The question is how studies have made methods choices, not what the vaccine's effectiveness is, so a scoping review that charts each choice fits. Choices vary widely and are often unreported (claim c1), test type has become a live choice since 2020 (claim c2), and post-2020 studies differ on SARS-CoV-2-positive controls (claim c4). The review follows JBI scoping review methods and PRISMA-ScR.
alternatives: Systematic review with meta-analysis of effectiveness estimates (refused: the question is methods, not a pooled estimate)
Write the protocol from the methods overview alone (refused: the overview predates post-2020 practice)
whyNotMoreComplex: Pooling estimates across studies that made different choices would hide the variation the protocol needs to see.

decision.statement: Run a scoping review of methods choices in test-negative influenza vaccine effectiveness studies from 2010 onward, charting case definition, test type, specimen timing, calendar time, repeat testing, prior vaccination, vaccination source and SARS-CoV-2-positive controls, because these choices vary widely (c1), test type has become a live choice since 2020 (c2) and post-2020 control selection is inconsistent (c4).
decision.question: How have published test-negative studies made the methods choices the agency's protocol must make?

criteria.text: Methods choices vary widely and are inconsistently reported.
Rapid antigen testing has become common since 2020 and misclassifies cases, so test type must be charted.
Studies since 2021 differ on SARS-CoV-2-positive controls.
A current scoping review of these methods choices already exists.

gates.evidence: Registration OSR-2026-7731 dated 2026-09-12, supplied by the investigator
Library request ALIB-2026-58, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Systematic review with meta-analysis of effectiveness estimates (refused: the question is methods, not a pooled estimate)
Write the protocol from the methods overview alone
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2 and c4 from retrieved records; both gates rest on the investigator's records.

summary: Scoping review recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
